title: Power Automate: AI-assisted UI automation repair in the desktop flow designer
summary: Hold: the governance checklist sends readers to solution history for selector changes, but Microsoft documents solution operations there, not selector comparisons. The feedback API entry is not a runnable command, and the proposed maker-group enablement is not documented. The feature description, roadmap dates and preview licensing are supported.

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified on 2026-10-27T23:05:02.
A new agentic debug run opens a repair interface while the flow runs.
claims.quote: A new agentic debug run feature will be available in the flow designer. The UI automation repair interface launches while the flow is running

claims.claim: The debug run validates each selector used in the flow.
claims.quote: validating each selector used in the flow

claims.claim: When an existing selector fails, the interface proposes a replacement after the maker captures the element.
claims.quote: It then proposes a new selector in case an existing one does not work as expected, after the user captures the respective element for reference.

claims.where: title; What's changing; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: This capability helps makers repair UI and browser automation in Power Automate for desktop.
claims.quote: AI-assisted UI automation repair (preview) in Power Automate for desktop is an AI-powered capability that helps makers repair UI and browser automation actions when selector-related failures occur during debugging.

claims.claim: The maker starts debugging with Run with AI-assisted UI Automation Repair in the flow designer.
claims.quote: In the flow designer, select the option Run with AI-assisted UI Automation Repair to start debugging the flow with the AI system's assistance.

claims.claim: The maker can review, edit and test the proposed selector.
claims.quote: Review, edit, and test the proposed selector.

claims.claim: The maker can accept the proposal, recapture the element or skip the suggestion.
claims.quote: Accept the selector, recapture the UI element to repeat the process, or skip the suggestion.

claims.claim: Learn documents AI-assisted UI automation repair as a preview feature.
claims.quote: This is a preview feature.

claims.claim: Power Automate for desktop version 2.70 or later is required.
claims.quote: You need version 2.70 or higher for Power Automate for desktop.

claims.claim: Application or web-page UI changes can cause selector failures and maintenance work.
claims.quote: Flows with UI and web automation actions often require maintenance when: Desktop applications or web pages change their UI structure. Existing selectors no longer uniquely identify the intended element.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The feature analyzes the failing selector and a newly captured selector of the intended UI element.
claims.quote: the feature analyzes the failing selector together with a newly captured selector of the same UI element and proposes a more resilient selector that makers can review, test, and apply.

claims.claim: Repaired selectors change production-flow behavior once saved.
claims.quote: Save draft: Save your latest changes without releasing them as the official version. ... Publish: Set a version as official so it runs from the console or cloud.
claims.fix: Replace 'Repaired selectors change the behaviour of production flows once saved.' with 'Selector changes are permanently saved when the maker saves the flow.' The repair article supports persistence, not the claim that saving alone updates production execution in environments with version control.

claims.claim: Accepting a suggested selector updates the affected action.
claims.quote: If the maker accepts the suggested selector, it's added to the selectors list of the affected element, so that the action is updated accordingly and the flow can continue to run.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: AI-assisted UI automation repair runs only through the flow designer during debugging.
claims.quote: AI-assisted UI automation repair is a debugging capability, available only through the flow designer. It doesn't automatically repair selectors during unattended or attended runtime execution.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes no new identity or permission model for this repair feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "AI-assisted UI automation repair" "identity" "languages" "general availability". Opened the repair article, including prerequisites and required admin configuration; no new identity or permission model is specified.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Applying a repair requires maker capture and approval rather than autonomous modification.
claims.quote: The maker recaptures the intended UI element. ... Requires user review and approval before it applies selector changes. Doesn't automatically modify flows without user interaction.

claims.claim: Skipping a suggestion without error handling stops the debugging run.
claims.quote: If you skip the suggestion and no error handling is in place, the run throws an error and the AI-assisted debugging run stops.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The preview is included for organization premium accounts at no extra cost.
claims.quote: AI-assisted UI automation repair in Power Automate for desktop is currently available for organization premium accounts at no extra cost.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Usage might be subject to service limits or changes.
claims.quote: Usage might be subject to service limits or changes.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: General availability pricing, licensing and any Copilot Credits requirement have not yet been published for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "AI-assisted UI automation repair" pricing general availability credits admin disable. Opened the repair article and read licensing search results; only current preview no-extra-cost terms were found, not GA pricing or credit requirements.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: AI-assisted repair requires the shared Copilot in Power Automate admin setting.
claims.quote: requires the same Copilot prerequisite as other AI-powered capabilities in Power Automate: ... Under the Power Automate section, select Copilot in Power Automate, and then enable the On check box

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The feature-specific arrival default is unknown, including the initial state of its shared prerequisite for this preview.
claims.quote: Searched: "AI-assisted UI automation repair" "default" "setting". Read the roadmap, repair article and Copilot overview. The feature article gives an enablement prerequisite, not its arrival default; the overview's broader defaults do not settle this preview's environment setting.

claims.claim: Other Copilot in Power Automate for desktop capabilities have regional and account-type restrictions.
claims.quote: Create flows using Copilot (preview) - United States ... Currently, Copilot in Power Automate for desktop is only available for users with a work or school account.

claims.claim: The documented path is Power Platform admin center > Copilot > Settings > Power Automate > Copilot in Power Automate > On.
claims.quote: In Power Platform admin center, go to Copilot > Settings. Under the Power Automate section, select Copilot in Power Automate, and then enable the On check box in the displayed pane.

claims.claim: An API equivalent for the environment-level Copilot in Power Automate prerequisite is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot in Power Automate" "Set-Environment" API setting repair. Read repair, Copilot hub, overview and List tenant settings. The latter's disableCopilot explicitly governs cloud flows, not a documented API for this desktop-repair prerequisite.

claims.claim: Runtime repair configuration is under Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Desktop flow repair at runtime configuration in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: select Manage. ... select Environments. ... select an environment. ... select Settings. ... Expand Product, and then select Features. ... Desktop flow repair at runtime configuration (preview)

claims.claim: The runtime configuration governs the separate preview Repair with Copilot capability.
claims.quote: Find the Repair at runtime setting for the desired run mode (attended and unattended) under the Desktop flow repair at runtime configuration setting in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: An API equivalent for Desktop flow repair at runtime configuration is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Desktop flow repair at runtime" API PowerShell setting. Opened Manage feature settings, Repair flow automation errors and search results; found UI configuration and feedback automation, not an API for the runtime-repair flag.

claims.claim: Manage > Tenant settings opens the tenant settings page in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Manage. In the Manage pane, select Tenant settings.

claims.claim: The API column supplies 'disableSurveyFeedback governance setting for Power Automate for desktop' as the automation call.
claims.quote: Searched: "disableSurveyFeedback" "Set-TenantSettings". Opened desktop governance, Set-TenantSettings and List tenant settings. disableSurveyFeedback exists, contrary to the pre-check lead, but this phrase specifies no executable operation, parameters or value.
claims.fix: Remove the feedback control row from the controls array and rendered table, retaining the existing prose about the documented disableSurveyFeedback tenant setting. The supplied phrase is not a call under the schema's runnable-call requirement; do not replace it with a claim that no automation exists, since governance links to Set-TenantSettings.

claims.claim: The desktop Copilot page names a tenant-level Copilot feedback control for preventing feedback to Microsoft.
claims.quote: As a Power Platform admin, you can prevent users from sending Copilot feedback to Microsoft by using the "Copilot feedback" tenant setting.

claims.claim: Additional Copilot feedback on the Tenant settings page is described specifically for Copilot in Power Apps.
claims.quote: Additional Copilot feedback | When using Copilot in Power Apps, allows users to share their prompts, questions, and requests with Microsoft.

claims.where: controls[3]; Governance controls table; Open questions
claims.claim: No dedicated admin UI or API switch specific to designer AI-assisted repair is documented beyond the shared prerequisite.
claims.quote: Searched: "AI-assisted UI automation repair" "admin" "API" "disable". Read the feature's full configuration section, desktop governance and search results; found the shared Copilot prerequisite and maker run option, not a dedicated admin switch.

claims.claim: The shared Copilot setting can be enabled specifically for a pilot group of makers.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot in Power Automate" setting specific users security group. Opened the repair article and Copilot hub. Configuration is described for environments or environment groups, not a maker-group audience for this setting.
claims.fix: Replace 'Enable the setting for a pilot group of makers first.' with 'Pilot use with a small group of makers; the documented Copilot setting is environment-scoped, not a documented maker-group switch.'

claims.claim: Saved selector changes can be reviewed in solution history.
claims.quote: An operation can be a solution import, export, or uninstall. The solution history displays information such as solution version, solution publisher, type of operation, operation start and end time, and operation status.
claims.fix: Replace 'Review saved selector changes in solution history.' with 'Review saved selector changes before wider use.' Solution history records solution operations; it is not the desktop-flow version comparison surface.

claims.claim: Microsoft's desktop governance page directs admins to contact Microsoft Support to disable all Copilot capabilities.
claims.quote: To prevent your users from using any copilot capability contact Microsoft Customer Support to disable all copilot functionality in your tenant.

claims.claim: The Copilot hub documents environment and environment-group settings.
claims.quote: You can configure settings at the environment level, with most settings also configurable through environment groups and rules.

claims.claim: The Copilot overview describes tenant-level disabling and says environment-level support is unavailable, unlike the Copilot hub guidance.
claims.quote: an admin needs to contact support and they use a PowerShell script to turn it off only at tenant level. Environment level support isn't available.

claims.claim: The Copilot overview describes cross-geo data sharing as the control for Copilot in regions without GPUs.
claims.quote: If a region doesn't have GPUs (everywhere else except sovereign clouds), Microsoft turns on Copilot by default by toggling on the cross-geo data sharing.

claims.claim: Self-healing is a separately enabled runtime capability rather than designer AI-assisted repair.
claims.quote: Self-healing is a runtime-only capability. ... has no effect during designer runs. ... Enable self-healing per action: ... Open the Error handling settings. Turn on Self-healing (Preview).

claims.claim: The desktop governance page identifies disableSurveyFeedback as a tenant setting for preventing Copilot-related feedback.
claims.quote: As a Power Platform admin you can prevent users from sending feedback to Microsoft by disabling the disableSurveyFeedback tenant setting.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not explicitly equate the desktop Copilot feedback UI setting with disableSurveyFeedback.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot feedback" "disableSurveyFeedback" "desktop". Read desktop Copilot, governance, Tenant settings and List tenant settings; the pages name controls but do not explicitly map that desktop UI label to disableSurveyFeedback.

claims.claim: The general availability region and language coverage for this feature remains unspecified.
claims.quote: Searched: "AI-assisted UI automation repair" "identity" "languages" "general availability". Opened the repair article and read search results; the article describes current preview cloud restrictions, not a GA region or language commitment.
